about: Corrections the owner's relationship decisions need and the review list cannot hold, read by `python scripts/relationships.py decide` on every run, so that a correction made once is applied on every later run and a run with no flags writes what the last one wrote. The eight keys are the command's eight flags, each keyed by a BibleData row id of the fact: reference (the verse to write the clause with: one verse, a passage of up to three, or two verses joined by a semicolon), relation (the vocabulary word the fact is read in), hold, flip, unsure (the confidence of a fact the owner accepts but says the verse does not settle), people (the people a gentilic makes him one of), reason (what the written clause says for itself) and owner (the date the owner ruled himself on a fact an agent decided). A flag given on the command line is written into this file and wins over it for the same row. Each correction is what a note on the decision in bibledata-relationships.json asks for, the owner's or the agent's he set to it; the *Why keys say which.
referenceWhy: BibleData cites the verse of a son's birth in Genesis 30 and 35, where he is 'a son' and not yet named: the verse names neither end of the tie, and a clause cites a verse its subject is named in. The next verse names him (Naphtali GEN 30:8, Zebulun 30:20, Joseph 30:24, Benjamin 35:18), and the clause is written there, on his record. Abram and Sarai (GEN 20:12) are not here: no verse naming either of them states that she is his father's daughter. Where BibleData cites a verse that does not name the person, or the owner names another: Zetham and Joel, whom BibleData makes Jehiel's sons citing 1CH 25:22 (which names neither), at 1CH 23:8, where the owner reads them as Jehiel's brothers; Eliashib the singer at EZR 10:24 (BibleData cites 10:23, the verse before); Eliezer, descendant of Levi, at EZR 10:18, as the owner's note '10:18' says. Under the owner's rules of 2026-09-29 (a passage of up to three verses naming both people, or two verses each stating a part): Jezreel, son of Hosea, at HOS 1:2-4, where 1:2 names Hosea and 1:4 Jezreel (1:3-4, as the owner cited it, does not name Hosea); Shebaniah of the Levites at NEH 10:9-10, the heading and the line he stands in (this Shebaniah is the one of 10:10, not 10:12); Athaliah, wife of Jehoram, at 2KI 8:18 with 8:26; Bunni, descendant of Merari, at NEH 11:15 with 1CH 9:14; Cush the Benjamite at the title of Psalm 7, which the canonical frame numbers 7:0; Zetham at 1CH 23:8; Simeon, half-brother of Benjamin, at GEN 35:22-24, the list of Jacob's sons by their mothers; Abram, half-brother of Sarai, at GEN 20:12-14, Abraham's answer to Abimelech and Sarah restored to him; Meonothai, son of Othniel, at 1CH 4:13-14 as the owner cited it. Under the owner's rule of 2026-09-29 that a passage and a verse elsewhere may be joined, each stating its part: Sarai, daughter of Terah, at GEN 20:12-14 with GEN 11:27 (she is Abraham's father's daughter; Terah is Abram's father). Hiram, of the Naphtalites, at 1KI 7:13-14: 7:13 names him and 7:14 the tribe, since 7:14 calls him only 'a widow's son'. Zechariah, grandson of Iddo, at ZEC 1:1, the verse that names Berechiah between them; EZR 5:1 calls him 'the son of Iddo'. Amnon, who forced Tamar, at 2SA 13:12-14 with 2SA 13:22: the passage the owner cited tells it and names neither of them, 13:22 names both and says it again.
relationWhy: The note names the right word where the dataset's is wrong, and a removal or re-ask so corrected is a confirmation. The owner's: Salu, descendant of Simeon ('not son, but descendant'); Ishbi-benob, descendant of Rapha; Kish, son of Abiel, not grandson; Amminadab, son of Ram ('Aram begat Amminadab'); Ephraim, ancestor of Telah and of Ammihud; Sisera, Jabin's commander, not Jabin king of Sisera. The agent's: Tohu, grandson of Elkanah (1CH 6:34-35); Tahath, Zabad and Ladan, descendants of Ephraim down a 'his son' chain (1CH 7:20-26); Benaiah the Pirathonite, descendant of Ephraim (1CH 27:14). The owner's of 2026-09-29: Zetham is Jehiel's brother (1CH 23:8), and 'the sons of Jehieli' in 26:22 is the clan's name. Joel is Jehiel's brother as Zetham is (1CH 23:8), the owner's of 2026-09-29. Gershom is Manasseh's son (JDG 18:30), the owner's of 2026-09-29: BibleData states the tie the other way round, so its rows are removed and the fact is written from Gershom's end.
holdWhy: A fact waits here when its note questions who is meant, or when the owner asked for the text to be checked before his decision is applied and the text does not say what the decision would write. None waits now. Manasseh, descendant of Ben-geber (72591), and Meonothai, son of Othniel (73281), the owner kept on 2026-09-29 once the Hebrew was put to him: 1KI 4:13 gives Ben-geber 'the towns of Jair the son of Manasseh' (חַוֹּת יָאִיר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁה); 1CH 4:13 in BHSA reads 'and the sons of Othniel: Hathath' (וּבְנֵי עָתְנִיאֵל חֲתַת), which he reads as shortened, since 4:14 goes on to Meonothai and the Vulgate and the Berean name him in 4:13. James son of Mary (76119), held before, the owner removed on 2026-09-28: no verse makes the brothers of Jesus Mary's sons.
flipWhy: The dataset states the tie from the end the note reads it from the other way: Sisera is defined as Jabin's commander, and the agent's note reverses Ephraim 'descendant of Benaiah' into Benaiah of the children of Ephraim. Gershom, son of Manasseh: BibleData makes Manasseh Gershom's son, and the owner reads Judges 18:30 the other way (2026-09-29).
unsureWhy: The owner accepts the fact but says the verse does not settle it. 0.5: Eshcol and Aner as Amorites, Abital as David's wife who may be a concubine, Rimmon of Benjamin ('not exact'). 0.9: Doeg and Ahimelech, Gilead and Hammolecheth ('high confidence, not absolute'), and his ruling in chat of 2026-09-27 that a man the verse calls a priest is Aaron's descendant, not certainly. Of 2026-09-28 in the console: 0.9 for the nine Levites of 2CH 31:13 he marked 'very likely', and 0.5 for Hammedatha, descendant of Agag (EST 3:1), which he marked 'let's use it as unsure'.

peopleWhy: A gentilic is membership of the people, not descent from the eponym (the owner, 2026-09-29): Cush the Benjamite (Psalm 7) of the Benjaminites, and Shebaniah of the Levites under the heading 'And the Levites' (NEH 10:9), each in place of BibleData's descent from Benjamin and from Levi. reasonWhy: The reason a written clause carries, which the page shows beside it, where the decision's note is a question or the agent's working rather than what the verse says.
